title: Dependability Cohort: Guardrails & Decision Playbook
summary: Working plan for a cohort-based SLO adoption program. Focus: lightweight guardrails, decision authority matrix, micro-experiments for measurement, and friction-reduced runbooks for feature teams.
content:
Purpose
---
Context: we need a way to operationalize SLOs across 10–12 pilot services without heavy central coordination. The cohort model bundles services that share traffic patterns and operational risk, letting us iterate quickly on runbooks, measurement signals, and escalation flows.

Goal (90 days): onboard 3 cohorts (total ~10 services) to a standardized SLO charter, shipped observability contracts, and a lightweight escalation path. Deliverables: SLO charters (per service), metric ownership table, a single-page playbook (this doc -> canonical), two canary micro-experiments for latency and error signal, and automations for alert-to-incident linkage.

Why cohort?
- Faster feedback (peer-to-peer learning).
- Shared instrumentation templates reduce rework.
- Easier risk grouping for rollback/fallback policies.

Scope & out-of-scope
- In-scope: API services and model-serving endpoints on hosted/dedicated infra; instrumentation of latency P95/P99, tail errors, token-level cost spikes, and cold-start indicators.
- Out-of-scope: batch jobs, data pipelines, and infra upgrade scheduling (handled by platform-eng).

Stakeholders & roles (quick map)
- Cohort Lead (SRE): Maya Patel (owner) — runs cadence, final decision on go/no-go for cohort gates.
- Service Leads: eng PM + tech lead for each service (see cohort roster).
- Observability SME: Ava Chen — templates, dashboards, query review.
- Reliability Product Partner: Diego Morales — exec syncs, success criteria.
- Incident Liaison: Liam O'Connor (oncall overlap & runbook reviewer).
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success liaison: Priya Kapoor — external customer impact review when needed.

Cohort composition (draft)
- Cohort A (low-latency frontends): 3 services (auth-proxy, session-store, routing-api).
- Cohort B (model-serving): 4 services (embed-encoder, generation-router, kv-cache, qcache-proxy).
- Cohort C (internal tools): 3 services (metrics-ingest, admin-api, billing-worker).
*Note: service names are placeholders; finalize with PMs in kickoff.*

Program timeline (high level)
Week 0: kickoff + charter template adoption; baseline metric export; pick cohort leads.
Week 1–3: instrumentation changes & dashboard templates landed (observability SME reviews).
Week 4: first micro-experiment (latency tail) for Cohort A; define SLO thresholds and error budgets.
Week 6: runbook draft reviews and tabletop exercise with oncall (Liam).
Week 8: second micro-experiment (error budget burn simulation) for Cohort B.
Week 10: cross-cohort retro; update playbook; decide on scale to remainder of org.

SLO Charter template (to copy into service docs)
- Service name: 
- Owner(s): 
- Primary signals: latency P95 / P99 (ms), availability (5xx/sec), correct-response ratio (%), queuing-time (ms)
- SLO statement: "Over a 30d window, the service should meet latency P95 < X ms and availability >= Y% excluding planned maintenance."
- Measurement window: rolling 30d / 7d for fast-feedback
- Error budget policy: allow automated throttles only after 60% budget burn in 24h; human approval required at 80%
- Escalation path: automatic alert -> paging -> runbook -> SLA review meeting
- Rollback criteria: defined by error budget + customer impact score > 6/10

Decision authority matrix (condensed)
- Metric interpretation: Observability SME + Service Lead must agree on signal validity.
- SLO threshold changes: Service Lead proposes; Cohort Lead approves; Reliability Product notifies executive sponsors.
- Emergency rollback: Service Lead + SRE oncall can action; Cohort Lead documents within 24h.

Micro-experiments (design notes)
1) Latency-tail canary (14 days)
- Goal: validate P99 sensitivity to batching and cache warmup.
- Method: route 5% traffic to a variant with mid-size batch window + KV cache priming; collect P95/P99 delta and token cost delta.
- Success criteria: P99 reduced by >= 15% without >5% increase in token cost.
- Safety: auto-fail on 1.5x error rate.

2) Error-budget burn simulation (chaos-lite)
- Goal: ensure runbooks map to real-world mitigation steps and that escalations run end-to-end.
- Method: synthetic traffic spike + injected transient 502 on one downstream for 30m. Observe detection, pager time-to-ack, and mitigation path.
- Success criteria: detection <5m, mitigation action taken <15m, customer-visible error <1% of normal load.

Observability contracts (minimal)
- Metrics: standardized names and units (latency_ms.p95, latency_ms.p99, errors.5xx.rate, cache.hit_rate).
- Dashboards: one-liner summary + drilldowns for tail latency, queued requests, dependency graph.
- Alerts: threshold-based + anomaly detector for residuals; alert includes runbook link and suggested mitigations.

Runbook composition checklist (for each service)
- One-line symptom-to-action map.
- Quick triage checklist (3 steps).
- Top 3 mitigation levers (e.g., reduce batch, increase pool, enable fallback model).
- Rollback steps and known side-effects.
- Postmortem owner & SLAs for documentation.

Communications plan
- Weekly cohort sync (30m) — progress updates + blockers.
- Biweekly cross-cohort show-and-tell (60m) — lessons, dashboards, experiment outcomes.
- Exec update: short scoreboard at end of each cohort (Diego prepares).
- Customer comms: CS/Solutions to draft templated messaging (Priya).

Risk assessment & mitigation (quick heatmap)
- Instrumentation gaps: high risk -> allocate 2-day observability hack sprint.
- Cross-service dependency surprise: medium -> require dependency mapping before experiment.
- False positives in alerts: medium -> add anomaly suppression and signal validation step.

Success metrics (how we know we shipped well)
- 10 services onboarded into Cohort program with charters and runbooks.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) < 5m for cohorted services.
- Error budget automation triggered safely in at least 1 live incident with correct mitigation path.
- Reduction in 90th->99th latency gap by >=10% across model-serving cohort.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Finalize cohort roster with PMs by next Tues (JIRA: SREPROG-412).
- Do we need a legal review for any customer-impacting throttles? (Priya to check).
- Who owns the canonical dashboard URL? (Ava to propose).
- Can platform-eng pre-reserve extra capacity for experiments? (ask platform-eng).

Appendix A — quick table: artifacts to produce
- SLO charter (per service) -> doc link
- Observability template (metrics & dashboard) -> github/infra/observability#289
- Runbook single page -> stored in /runbooks/cohort-a/ etc.
- Experiment configs -> airflow or feature-flag repo (owner: service lead)

Meeting cadence (operationalization)
- Daily 15-min hotseat during micro-experiments (optional for teams in active window).
- Weekly sync (everyone) — unblock and commit next steps.
- Monthly steering review (executive digest).

Quick scratch checklist for cohort kickoff (copy into calendar invite)
- Invite: Service Leads, SRE Cohort Lead, Observability SME, Product reliability partner, CS liaison, Platform eng rep.
- Agenda: goals, charter template walkthrough, timeline, initial blockers, next actions.
- Deliverable at end: signed SLO charter draft + instrumentation PRs assigned.

Notes (informal)
- Keep the first cohort light — prefer wins that are measurable and low-risk.
- Document every alert change; small noisy alerts are the worst time-sink.
- We'll keep a short public (internal) scoreboard in the Console to show progress — helps sell to PMs.

References & useful links
